query: How does incident resolution efficiency vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: problem_domain
per_column.rationale: A small set of clean, well-separated interpretable categories (hardware, software, network, infrastructure) that can be segmented and compared against resolution efficiency. Partly overlaps with existing 'category' but adds an external associational lens.

per_column.name: equipment_type
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-populated categories (printer, monitor, keyboard, etc.) that support meaningful grouping; efficiency likely varies by equipment type, enabling relationship discovery.

per_column.name: root_cause_type
per_column.rationale: Clear, interpretable causal categories that are strongly associational with resolution efficiency and easy to segment on for a human explorer.

per_column.name: assigned_team_member
per_column.rationale: Essentially duplicates the existing 'assigned_to' field and overlaps with assignment_group, which is already a query dimension. It restates the assignment focus rather than opening a new external relationship.

per_column.name: incident_recurrence
per_column.rationale: A clean binary flag with a reasonable split (423/77) that offers an informative, interpretable segmentation; recurring vs. non-recurring incidents plausibly differ in resolution efficiency.

judge.rationale: As a set, the added columns provide several interpretable, well-separated categorical segmentations (problem_domain, equipment_type, root_cause_type, incident_recurrence) that a human can group on and compare against resolution efficiency, supporting genuine exploratory analysis. They avoid opaque scores and near-constant values. The main weaknesses are that 'assigned_team_member' largely restates the pre-existing assignment fields, and problem_domain partially overlaps with the existing 'category' dimension, so novelty is modest. Overall the set meaningfully opens up informative relationships around the focus.
